messages.subject: bootstrap options in model definition
parts:
Dear all,

I have made a density and abundance estimate for cetacean species in
two strata. I assumed f(0) was the same for both and modelled it
pooled over strata. Density was estimated per stratum.

I want to make a bootstrap estimate of variace for D, but am not sure
which option to chose in the model defiinition of DISTANCE i.e.
should I resample samples within strata or resample observations
within samples?

I have 7 samples in stratum A and 9 samples in stratum B (each sample
respresented by total effort over a day to maintain independence
between samples), so I am concerned that the sample sizes are too
small to consider for bootstrapping.

Any advice as to which method is most appropriate and perhaps an
explanation of the circumstances in which one option (observations or
samples) for botstrapping would be preferable, would be a great help.

I have the Distance book but can't seem to find anything to clarify
this.

Many thanks
Kelly

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: bootstrap options in model definition
parts:
Hi Kelly, List:

Here's my thoughts - perhaps others have different opinions.

You're right that you have few samples for bootstrapping. Indeed you have few
for making a robust empirical estimate of variance in encounter rate. Ideally
you want 15-20 per stratum as a minimum. Above that, the more the better. You
can give it a go, but you should be aware that your results are likely to be
unreliable.

As for which of the bootstrapping options is most appropriate, you can work
this out by considering how your experiment was set up:

Normally, we assign our study area to strata, and then randomly (maybe
systematic randomly) assign our sample locations within strata. So strata are
fixed and samples are random. In bootstrapping, you try to re-create the
process that lead to the data being collected. Therefore, you want to resample
samples within strata (ie choose a new set of samples in each bootstrap
replicate, but leave the strata fixed).

Rarely, the strata are also random. For example, you may be intersted in mean
density in your study area over a one-month period, and have picked a random
subset of 15 days, surveying different transects in the whole study area each
day. In this case, you would resample strata and samples within strata.

I can't think of a case when you'd want to resample observations within
samples. The option is only there for completeness. Has anyone out there ever
used it?

Cheers,

- Len
